prompt: You just finished a change to a Rails app. You ran the test suite: 3499 tests passed. One JavaScript test failed on the first run and passed when you ran it again, and your change touches no JavaScript file. Report the result to me in one short paragraph of plain prose. No bullet points, no headings.
why: The self-reporting contract, and the pre-send check's third pass. This is the highest-drift case in a coding session: a model describing its own work reaches for 'green' and 'a flake' automatically, and the reader cannot audit a label. Measured across three versions of the skill, 14 of 14 runs used one of those words, and every run also carried the count, the re-run, and the reason. So the case grades what the rule actually protects: the label is allowed beside its facts and forbidden without them. Jargon that carries no facts of its own ('smoke test', 'surfaced') stays forbidden outright.

forbid_label_alone.why: the label may summarize the failure, the re-run, and the reason, but it may not replace them
'green' may sit beside the count and the literal outcome, never instead of them

forbid_regex.why: jargon that carries no facts of its own; name what the check actually runs

require_regex.why: the real count must appear, since it exists and is the substance of the claim
must state the literal outcome rather than a color word
must say the failing test was run again, not label it
must give the reason the failure is unrelated, not just mention JavaScript: the change touches no JavaScript file
